```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`call_scn()` returns a `scphasedcn` object; `write_scphasedcn(res, out)` writes it as flat tables (the command line does
both). `read_scphasedcn(out)` reads a written run back.

## Files

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `cells.tsv` | one row per called cell: cell type, depth stratum, null cell flag, `n_calls`, `n_events`, and the `multiplet` flag (normal mode always; tumour mode when `multiplets` are given: the cells above its `multiplet_prob`); tumour mode adds `clone`, `posterior`, `doublet_like`, `ref_pool` |
| `calls.tsv` | per cell x region calls (normal mode: the called rows; tumour mode: every clone row and every per-cell inherited / confirmed row) |
| `pooled_calls.tsv` | normal mode: called rows of the cell pools (named `event` regions only with `pool_events`, off by default: experimental, not calibrated per event) |
| `events.tsv` | a cell's overlapping called regions merged into events (normal mode: with `null_cell`, `p`, `q`, `null_borrowed`; `q` is descriptive, not a false discovery rate, see [False-event load](#false-event-load-normal-mode)) |
| `thresholds.tsv` | the null thresholds per score, region class and depth stratum (and cross-validation fold); named `event` regions have no null rows of their own and use the thresholds of their `sd_class` (column `borrowed_from`, present when a run has events; the pooled ones only with `pool_events`) |
| `regions.tsv` | the regions scored (arms, chromosomes, 5-50 Mb tiles, events; tumour mode also clone pieces) |
| `null_fit.tsv` | the depth null (Student-t per class x stratum) and the allelic overdispersion `rho` |
| `false_calls.tsv`, `false_events.tsv` | normal mode: the realised false-call rate on the null cells |
| `expected_false.tsv` | normal mode: expected false calls and events per class x state (`event_fdr()`; lower bounds) |
| `null_selection_check.tsv` | normal mode with `call_scn(null_check = TRUE)` / `--null-check`: the selection-free check of the per-cell null (`null_selection_check()`) |
| `clones.tsv`, `assignments.tsv`, `clone_segments.tsv`, `clone_profiles.tsv.gz`, `reference_pool.txt` | tumour mode: clones, per-cell assignment, clone copy-number segments, clone window profiles, the normal reference cells |
| `summary.tsv` | headline numbers (`scphasedcn_summary()`) |
| `params.yaml` | every parameter of the run; reads back with `caller_params("params.yaml")` |
| `NOTES.md` | the run notes (inputs, steps, run time, package version) |
| `result.rds` | the object without the large `scores` / `features` tables |
| `scores.tsv.gz`, `features.tsv.gz` | optional (`write_scores`, `write_features`; large) |

## Calls

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `cell` | the cell (normal mode pools: the pool id; tumour mode clone rows: the clone) |
| `region`, `class`, `chrom`, `start`, `end` | the region (0-based, half-open) and its class: `arm`, `chrom`, `5Mb` ... `50Mb`, `event` |
| `state` | `loss` (1:0), `gain` (2:1), `cnloh` (2:0, copy-neutral LOH), `gain_as`, `amp`, `del`, `neutral`, or a clone state label |
| `score`, `thr`, `called` | the region score, its null threshold and `score > thr` |
| `level` | `cell`, `pool` or `clone` |
| `source` | `cell` (the cell's own evidence), `inherited` (from its clone or pool) or `confirmed` (a clone call the cell's own evidence confirms) |
| `reportable` | the call survives the nesting rules (e.g. a chromosome gain is not reported inside a stronger nested arm loss) |
| `z`, `f`, `n_hap` | normal mode, cell rows: depth z, major-haplotype fraction and molecule votes of the cell in the region (not in tumour mode) |
| `stratum` | normal mode, cell rows: the cell's depth stratum (clean fragments; `<20k`, `20-50k`, `>=50k`; not in tumour mode) |
| `p`, `q`, `null_borrowed` | normal mode, tested per-cell rows: the empirical p-value against the null rows, the row-level Benjamini-Hochberg q-value (descriptive: not a false discovery rate, not a filter) and whether the row's chromosome (chrX) or class has no null rows of its own (see below); NA on other rows |
| `confident` | tumour mode: the cell's clone assignment is confident |

## False-event load (normal mode)

Normal mode calls a cell-region when its score exceeds the 1 / 1,000 quantile of the null rows of its class and depth
stratum (`null_q`). The budget is per cell-region, and a cell has about a hundred reportable rows (chromosomes, arms,
50 Mb tiles), so among thousands of cells a run carries a predictable number of false per-cell events. `event_fdr()`
(run by `call_scn()`) makes that number visible; it changes no call, threshold or score.

**Expected false calls and events** (`expected_false.tsv`, one row per class x state x chromosome group):

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `class`, `state` | the reportable per-cell class x state (e.g. `chrom` `gain`, `arm` `loss`) |
| `chrom_group` | `A` (autosomes), `X`, `Y` |
| `null_borrowed` | the rate comes from the autosomal null rows (chrX rows are never null rows), or from the `sd_class` of a class without null rows |
| `n_rows` | per-cell rows of the class (every cell x region; each one a null hypothesis) |
| `n_tested` | of these, the rows whose best state is this state and that would be reportable if called (calling policy, gain depth gate) |
| `n_called`, `n_events` | reportable called rows of this state; events whose top region is of this class and state |
| `n_null`, `n_null_called`, `n_null_events`, `null_per_1000` | null rows of the class, how many of them are reportable calls of this state (fold-cross-validated thresholds, policy and gain gate applied as for every cell), how many null-cell events have such a top region, and the call rate per 1,000 null rows |
| `expected_false_calls`, `expected_false_events` | the null rate per depth stratum x `n_rows` of that stratum, summed over the strata; `_lo` / `_hi`: 95 % Poisson interval of the null count |
| `false_frac_calls`, `false_frac_events` | expected false / called (capped at 1): the implied false proportion (a lower bound, see below) |

These are **lower bounds**. Every row counts as a null hypothesis, but the null rate is measured on the selected null
cells, which were chosen for having no chromosome or arm call at a stricter threshold (`select_null_cells()`). Their
rows are cleaner than those of an unselected normal cell; when the parametric selection null is too thin (shared
allelic bias, noisier cells), the selection truncates the null tail and the realised false rate of the other cells is
higher. chrX rows (and their events) take the autosomal rate, which ignores X-inactivation driven allelic imbalance in
females. `summary.tsv` carries the headline: `events | cell_events_in_null_cells` (events found in the null cells
themselves; their chrX is not screened), `events | expected_false_cell_events` (and per chromosome group),
`events | expected_false_cell_event_fraction`, `calls | expected_false_reportable_cell_calls`.

**p- and q-values.** For every tested per-cell row (classes reportable per cell, plus 20 Mb rows promoted by the
nesting rule) `p` compares the score of a *reportable* call (the score when the row would be reportable if called,
else minus infinity) with the same statistic on the null rows of the row's threshold group, in the
cross-validation folds its threshold was trained on: `p = (1 + #{null >= score}) / (n + 1)` (a conformal p-value).
A named `event` region borrows the thresholds of its `sd_class`, and its rows are compared with the same null rows
(those of the sd_class group and folds), scored as event rows would be (`null_borrowed = TRUE`).
With `n` null rows `p` cannot go below `1 / (n + 1)`; a strong event would then get a q-value that only reflects how
many other events are as strong (with `m` tests no single event can reach a q below about `m / (n + 1)`, which is
above 1 on real data). Beyond the (51st) largest null score of the group, `p` therefore follows an exponential tail
fitted to the top 50 null scores times the reportable share of that tail (`event_fdr(tail = "none")` gives the plain
conformal p-value; `summary.tsv` `events | empirical_p_floor` reports the floor). `q` is the Benjamini-Hochberg
q-value over all tested rows, called or not. In `events.tsv`, `p` / `q` / `null_borrowed` are those of the event's
top region and `null_cell` says whether the event is in a selected null cell. **`q` is a descriptive column: it is
not a false discovery rate and must not be used as a filter.** Two independent limits make it too small, and no
event-level q-value is computed:

- *Relative to the selected null.* `p`, and the exponential tail beyond the largest null scores, are computed against
  the selected null cells. The selection removes the cells with the heaviest tails (e.g. cells with more allelic
  overdispersion than modelled), so for cells like those `p` is too small and the tail model extrapolates a truncated
  distribution; the tail is conservative only for a correctly specified null with light tails. In a sample where
  part of the cells are noisier than the null cells, the default tail can give false events a small `q` that
  `event_fdr(tail = "none")` does not (on a simulated null in which 10 % of the cells had a higher allelic
  overdispersion, 28 events reached `q` < 0.05, all false; none with `tail = "none"`); compare the two when the null
  is in doubt.
- *Rows, not events.* Benjamini-Hochberg runs over rows, and one real event usually rejects several nested rows
  (chromosome, arms, tiles), while rows of one cell are positively dependent. A cut on `q` in `events.tsv` is
  therefore not an event-level false discovery rate: the share of false events below the cut can be well above it
  (in a simulation with 300 planted chromosome losses in 3,000 cells, 12 % of the events with `q` < 0.05 were
  false). The same holds for `summary.tsv` `events | cell_events_q_below_0.05`, a descriptive count of events at a
  row-level `q`.

**Selection-free check** (`null_selection_check.tsv`, `call_scn(null_check = TRUE)` / `--null-check`; it costs about
one more scoring pass). The autosomes are split into odd and even chromosomes; null cells are selected on one half
only, thresholds are trained as usual on that half's null rows, and exceedances are counted on the other half of the
same cells, rows that neither the selection nor the thresholds saw; then the halves swap. Per class x stratum (and
`all`): `n_rows`, `n_exceed`, `per_1000` with a 95 % Clopper-Pearson interval (`lo_per_1000`, `hi_per_1000`; rows of
one cell overlap, so the interval is somewhat narrow), `nominal_per_1000` (`1000 x (1 - null_q)`),
`insample_per_1000` (the cross-validated rate on the selection half of the same passes) and `cv_per_1000` (the
run's own in-sample rate, `false_calls.tsv`). Cells are selected on one half only, so a cell with a real event on
the measured half stays in and that event's rows count as exceedances: `per_1000` is the null rate plus the rate of
real events on the measured half, an upper bound of the null rate. A rate clearly above the nominal and in-sample
rates has two possible causes: a selected null that is cleaner than the cells it is applied to (the expected false
counts above are then too low), or real events. Read it next to the share of cells with a called event (`cells.tsv`
`n_events`, `summary.tsv`): in a sample without real events the excess measures the selection; in a sample with
them it is an upper bound. The halves carry different chromosomes, so a class whose regions differ in their null
spread shows up here as well.

## Clone segments (tumour mode)

`clone_segments.tsv`: per clone and segment `chrom`, `start`, `end`, `n_win` (1 Mb windows), the pooled oriented votes
`nA`, `nB`, the total copy number `cn`, the allele-specific state (`1:1`, `1:0`, `2:1`, `2:0`, `3:1`, ...), `log2`
(depth relative to the clone baseline), `f` (major-haplotype fraction), `llr`, `confident`, `label` (neutral, loss,
cnloh, gain, gain_as, amp, del) and `ploidy` (1 on a male's chrX / chrY). The clone `N0` is the fixed normal clone.

`assignments.tsv`: per cell the likelihood-best clone, its `posterior`, the margin to the second clone, whether the cell
looks like a doublet of two clones (`doublet_like`, `pair`, `p_mix`), and `confident` (posterior >= 0.9, not
doublet-like).

## The object

```{r object, message = FALSE}
library(scphasedcn)
library(data.table)
sim = simulate_scn(n_cells = 60, sex = "female", cell_types = c(a = 0.5, b = 0.5), events = NULL,
                   multiplet_rate = 0, depth = c(meanlog = log(12000), sdlog = 0.3), phase_block_mean = 1e9,
                   switch_rate = 2e-6, seed = 3)
d = file.path(tempdir(), "out_extract")
invisible(write_sim_dataset(sim, d))
cen = sim$scn$bins[, .(chrom, cstart = 1, len = max(end)), by = chrom][, .(chrom, cstart, cen_left = 0.4 * len,
                                                                             cen_right = 0.4 * len, cend = len)]
res = call_scn(d, "normal", sex = "female", centromeres = cen, null_cells = "select", verbose = FALSE)
names(res)
res$thresholds[level == "cell" & fold == 0][1:5, .(score, class, stratum, q, thr, n_null)]
out = file.path(tempdir(), "out_caller")
invisible(write_scphasedcn(res, out))
res2 = read_scphasedcn(out)
identical(res2$calls, res$calls)
```

The components of the object:

| component | normal mode | tumour mode |
|---|---|---|
| `cells` | cell, cell_type, stratum, fold, null_cell, multiplet | the cells with clone, posterior, ... |
| `regions` | the scored regions | the scored regions plus clone pieces |
| `scores` | per cell x region scores (with the null flag) | NULL |
| `thresholds` | per-cell (cross-validated) and pool thresholds (`level`) | per depth stratum and clone hypothesis |
| `calls`, `events` | see above | see above |
| `pools` | pool membership (`kind` = `type` or `knn`) | NULL |
| `clones`, `assignments`, `segments`, `profiles` | NULL | see above |
| `null_fit` | depth t parameters, rho, the null cells and how they were selected | depth t parameters, rho, reference pool, clone discovery details |
| `false_calls`, `false_events`, `expected_false`, `fdr_info`, `null_check` | null false-call rates, expected false calls / events, the q-value settings (tests, tail, calibration groups), the selection check (with `null_check = TRUE`) | NULL |
| `params` | all parameters, including the `normal:` caller arguments | all parameters, including the `tumour:` options |
| `features`, `feature_info`, `embedding`, `notes` | the per-cell region features and the run notes | the same |
